facts.statement: Psilopterus is an extinct genus of terror birds that lived in Argentina and Uruguay from the Middle Oligocene to possibly the Late Pleistocene.
facts.quote: Psilopterus (Greek for "bare wing") is an extinct genus of phorusrhacid ("terror bird") from the Middle Oligocene to possibly the Late Pleistocene of Argentina and Uruguay.

facts.statement: Members of the genus Psilopterus were relatively gracile and diminutive compared to other terror birds, including the smallest known species of terror bird.
facts.quote: Compared to other phorusrhacids, members of the genus are both relatively gracile and diminutive, and include the smallest known species of terror bird

facts.statement: Psilopterus birds resembled the modern cariama but had a heavier build and considerably smaller wings.
facts.quote: The birds resemble the modern cariama (Cariama cristata), except with a heavier build and considerably smaller wings.

facts.statement: The genus Psilopterus was described by Moreno and Mercerat in 1891.
facts.quote: authority: Moreno & Mercerat, 1891

facts.statement: Recent systematic revisions place Psilopterus within the subfamily Psilopterinae alongside the genera Procariama and Paleopsilopterus, divided into four species.
facts.quote: The most recent systematic revision of Phorusrhacidae placed Psilopterus within the subfamily Psilopterinae, along with the genera Procariama and Paleopsilopterus, and divided Psilopterus into four species.

facts.statement: It has been suggested that Psilopterus may have been able to fly briefly and clumsily, similar to extant seriemas, unlike larger terror birds.
facts.quote: It has been also suggested that, in contrast to the other larger terror birds, Psilopterus may have been able to fly, probably in a brief and clumsy manner like that of extant seriemas

facts.statement: Researchers suggest psilopterines likely preferred to run than fly, using flight primarily to reach treetops for nesting and protection from predators.
facts.quote: It is likely that psilopterines would have more preferred to run than fly, and that they would have utilized flight to reach the treetops for nesting and protection against predators.

facts.statement: Psilopterus bachmanni and lemoinei lived during the Middle Miocene in the Santa Cruz Formation, inhabiting coastal, forested, and grassland regions.
facts.quote: Psilopterus bachmanni and lemoinei lived during the middle Miocene in the Santa Cruz Formation, which preserves mostly a coastal environment, but also forested and grassland regions.

facts.statement: During the Miocene, the climate in the region was similar to the coasts of Chile, featuring semi-temperate forests and oceanic winds.
facts.quote: During the Miocene, the climate was similar to those of the coasts of Chile with semi-temperate forests and oceanic winds.

facts.statement: The environment included large herbivorous notoungulates like Nesodon and Adinotherium as low browsers, and the frugivorous interatheriid Protypotherium.
facts.quote: Large, herbivorous, South American notoungulate mammals like the toxodontids Nesodon and Adinotherium were the large low browsers, with rabbit-like interatheriiid Protypotherium being frugivorous.

facts.statement: It is debated whether material currently assigned to P. lemoinei and P. bachmanni may be reclassified into separate species if reexamined in depth.
facts.quote: A number of discrepancies between various specimens have been attributed to differences in age or sex, but material currently assigned to P. lemonei and P. bachmanni may be reclassified at the species level if reexamined in depth.

facts.statement: Psilopterus is an extinct genus of terror birds known in Greek as "naked wing".
facts.quote: Psilopterus (en idioma griego "ala desnuda") es un género extinto de fororrácido ("ave del terror")

facts.statement: Members of this genus were relatively slender and small compared to other terror birds.
facts.quote: Comparado con otros fororrácidos, los miembros de este género eran relativamente gráciles y pequeños

facts.statement: When standing on its head, P. bachmanni reached a height of 70 to 80 centimeters and weighed about 5 kilograms.
facts.quote: con la cabeza en alto P. bachmanni alcanzaba 70 - 80 centímetros de altura y pesaba cerca de 5 kilogramos

facts.statement: The largest members of the genus weighed only about 7 kilograms.
facts.quote: mientras que los mayores miembros del género solo alcanzaban 7 kilogramos

facts.statement: These birds resembled the modern Cariama cristata but had a more robust build and considerably smaller wings.
facts.quote: Estas aves recordaban a la actual cariama (Cariama cristata), excepto por su constitución más robusta y alas considerablemente menores

facts.statement: The morphological similarity between the claws of cariamas and Psilopterus suggests they were used to strike prey, as both are sharp, curved, and laterally compressed.
facts.quote: La gran similitud morfológica entre las garras de las cariamas y Psilopterus, siendo ambas afiladas, curvas y comprimidas lateralmente, pueden indicar que eran usadas para golpear a las presas

facts.statement: Researchers Tonni and Tambussi suggested Psilopterus could use its claws to climb trees and possibly fly, but this idea has been rejected in recent scientific literature.
facts.quote: Tonni y Tambussi también han sugerido que Psilopterus podría usar sus garras para trepar a los árboles, y podrían incluso volar; esta idea ha sido rechazada en la literatura científica más reciente

facts.statement: Psilopterus lived from the middle Oligocene to the late Pleistocene in Argentina.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del Oligoceno hasta finales del Pleistoceno superior en Argentina

facts.statement: Fossil finds in Uruguay suggest this genus may have survived until approximately 96,040 ± 6,300 years ago.
facts.quote: Hallazgos de fósiles de Uruguay indican que este género puede haber sobrevivido hasta hace apenas 96,040 ± 6,300 años

facts.statement: Recent systematic reviews place Psilopterus within the subfamily Psilopterinae of the family Phorusrhacidae.
facts.quote: La más reciente revisión sistemática de Phorusrhacidae sitúa a Psilopterus dentro de la subfamilia Psilopterinae

facts.statement: The genus Psilopterus is divided into four species.
facts.quote: y divide a Psilopterus en cuatro especies

facts.statement: Psilopterus bachmanni is one of the smallest terror bird species, rivaling only P. affinis in size.
facts.quote: Psilopterus bachmanni (Moreno & Mercerat, 1891) es una de las menores especies de fororrácidos, rivalizando solo con P. affinis

facts.statement: The species and genus were defined based on a fused upper ankle and a foot bone, with the lectotype being a tarsometatarsus (MLP-168).
facts.quote: Esta especie (y el género) se definió con la parte superior de un tobillo fusionado y un hueso del pie (el lectotipo MLP-168 es un tarsometatarso)

facts.statement: Material of this species comes from various sites in Santa Cruz province, Argentina, dating to the middle Miocene (Santacruciense).
facts.quote: El material procede de varios sitios de la provincia de Santa Cruz de Argentina que datan de mediados del Mioceno (Santacruciense)

facts.statement: Key diagnostic features include a low skull and an upper jaw similar to that of mesembriornithine terror birds.
facts.quote: Las características de diagnóstico más importantes son un cráneo bajo y una mandíbula superior (o maxilar; similar al de los fororrácidos mesembriornitinos)

facts.statement: Psilopterus lemoinei was contemporary with P. bachmanni and likely occupied a very similar ecological niche.
facts.quote: Psilopterus lemoinei (Moreno & Mercerat, 1891) es contemporáneo de P. bachmanni y probablemente llenaba un nicho ecológico muy similar

facts.statement: However, P. lemoinei was slightly larger, with an estimated average weight of 7 kilograms.
facts.quote: aunque P. lemoinei es levemente mayor, con un peso promedio estimado en 7 kilogramos

facts.statement: Diagnostic features include a high skull and a higher upper jaw.
facts.quote: Las características de diagnóstico incluyen un cráneo alto y una mandíbula más alta (maxilar)

facts.statement: Material of this species has been found in sites in Santa Cruz province, Argentina, dating to the middle Miocene (Santacruciense).
facts.quote: Dicho material se ha hallado en algunos sitios en la provincia de Santa Cruz de Argentina que datan de mediados del Mioceno (Santacruciense)

facts.statement: Psilopterus affinus is one of the least known terror bird species, represented only by part of a leg bone.
facts.quote: Psilopterus affinus (Ameghino, 1899) es una de las especies de ave del terror peor conocidas, representada solo por parte de un hueso de la pata

facts.statement: This bone indicates the bird was similar in size to P. bachmanni.
facts.quote: el cual indica que el ave era similar en talla a P. bachmanni

facts.statement: Specimens were found in 1899 in Chubut province, Argentina (Patagonia), in rocks dating from the middle to late Oligocene (Deseadense).
facts.quote: hallado en 1899 en la provincia de Chubut en Argentina (Patagonia), en rocas que datan de mediados a finales del Oligoceno (Deseadense)

facts.statement: Psilopterus colzecus is similar in size to P. lemoinei.
facts.quote: Psilopterus colzecus Tonni & Tambussi, 1988, es similar a P. lemoinei en tamaño

facts.statement: It is known from a single incomplete skeleton including parts of the jaw, wing, and leg, with the holotype being MLP-76-VI-12-2.
facts.quote: Conocido a partir de un único esqueleto incompleto que incluye partes de la mandíbula, el ala, y la pata (el holotipo MLP-76-VI-12-2)

facts.statement: The species is defined by a groove on the front of the thigh bone (trochlea).
facts.quote: La especie se define por un surco en el frente del hueso del muslo (troclea)

facts.statement: These elements were found in Buenos Aires province, Argentina, and date to the late Miocene (Chasiquense).
facts.quote: Estos elementos fueron hallados en la provincia de Buenos Aires de Argentina y datan del Mioceno Superior (Chasiquense)

facts.statement: The genus lived from the Aquitanian to the Late Pleistocene, approximately 23.04 to 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Late Pleistocene (23.04 to 0.0117 million years ago)
